newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: CA sale to start from scratch - Finmin.
newsitem.headline: CA sale to start from scratch - Finmin.

text.p: Austria's Finance Minister said on Monday the privatisation of Creditanstalt-Bankverein would start from scratch as he was unable to accept the bid made by an Austro-Italian-German consortium led by EA-Generali.
"I very much regret....that the offer put forward by the consortium on September 6 cannot be accepted," Viktor Klima said in a press statement.
Klima said that under sale conditions laid down in October 1995, the government envisaged selling its entire stake of around 19.9 million CA shares.
Moreover, the conditions sought to ensure the protection of national interests, improve the structure of Austria's banking sector, and guarantee "the best possible price" for the government's stake.

Klima said that in this respect the government's advisor, U.S. investment house J.P. Morgan, would work with CA to update the memorandum it produced in 1995 and come up with a new procedure for privatisation within a few weeks.
